text: In Ricoeur's account of mimesis, the configurational act (mise en intrigue) by which a narrative weaves diverse events and characters into a unified, followable whole with a beginning, middle, and end is called ___.
explanation: Emplotment (mise en intrigue) is Ricoeur's term for the configurational act at the heart of mimesis II (configuration), which transforms a mere sequence of events into a narrative whole. It is his practical response to the 'aporia of time' — the irreducible tension between subjective (Augustinian) and objective (Aristotelian) time — which narrative negotiates rather than dissolves. It is not prefiguration (mimesis I) or refiguration (mimesis III), the phases that flank it.
